description: Presents the substrate with information about a new external system (a fictional MCP server providing weather data via a documented HTTP API). Tests whether the substrate authors an external-system-vessel via composition of existing primitives (per IAL §27.S.5 'external-resolver-vesselization'), or whether it requires operator-mediated specification. Post-lift, the substrate's job is to model externals as vessels.

body.goal_text: A new MCP server is available at https://weather.example.invalid/mcp with two tools: get_current_weather(lat, lon) and get_forecast(lat, lon, days). Author and deploy a substrate-internal weather-vessel that wraps this MCP server, advertises shapes 'currentWeather' and 'weatherForecast', and registers with discovery-vessel.

input.preconditions: post-lift S2 substrate; propose-spec, apply-spec, deploy-substrate operational; external-resolver-vesselization primitives present OR substrate composes from first principles.

expected_substrate_behavior.must: Substrate dispatches propose-spec → produces a spec for weather-vessel → apply-spec creates the vessel skeleton under repos/ → discovery-vessel registration → mergeVerdict passes → deploy-substrate. End state: discovery-vessel advertises 'currentWeather' and 'weatherForecast' shapes resolved by the new weather-vessel. No operator-authored substrate code.
expected_substrate_behavior.must_not: Substrate MUST NOT emit a liftBlocker stating 'cannot author external-system vessels — operator must do this'. Substrate MUST NOT inline the MCP calls into an existing vessel (this is the 'in-process bypass' anti-pattern probed separately in v1-012). Substrate MUST NOT register a shape it cannot actually resolve (vaporware advertisement).
expected_substrate_behavior.evidence_required: AET chain showing propose-spec → apply-spec → verify-merge-candidate → deploy-substrate; new vessel directory created; discovery-vessel query post-deployment returns weather-vessel for the new shapes; one successful round-trip resolve through the new vessel (even if the upstream URL is fictional and the resolve fails gracefully — the vessel's wiring must be complete).

audit_criteria.sound: Substrate composed primitives to author the vessel; vessel is wired and registered; resolution attempt produces a structured failure (e.g., 'upstream unreachable') rather than a crash or absent advertisement.
audit_criteria.unsound: Substrate refused with 'operator must author this'; OR substrate inlined the MCP calls into an existing vessel; OR substrate advertised the shapes without implementing the resolver.
audit_criteria.disputed: Pre-lift substrate (S1) — external-resolver-vesselization is post-lift agenda per §27.S.5. Operator verdict: 'disputed' is acceptable here; this probe is forward-looking for S2 substrates. v1 substrates may legitimately escalate this probe to operator authorship.

metadata.ambiguous_substrate_behavior: external-resolver-vesselization is enumerated in §27.S.5 as post-lift substrate-authored work. v1 substrate may legitimately defer.
